hooks: Sustainability content on TikTok is one of two things: a girl with a perfectly aesthetic pantry, or someone yelling at me about my coffee cup. I'm doing this challenge for 30 days because I wanted a third option.
I make UGC for a living, which means I see every brand frame sustainability badly. So when one of them asked me to actually do a 30-day challenge, I went in fully skeptical.
I'm not a sustainability girlie. I recycle when I remember. I drive an old car. I order takeout. And I just signed up for a 30-day challenge to see what happens.
Day 1 of doing something I have zero qualifications for: a 30-day sustainability challenge as someone who is fully median at this.
Climate content makes me feel either guilty or fake-inspired, and I'm tired of both. So I'm trying a 30-day thing — out loud, on camera, without pretending I'm transformed.
coreAngle: Creator-marketer who is 'fully median' at sustainability does Phobaxx 30-day challenge — posting the honest version including the days she forgets, doesn't believe in it, and the days something actually clicks. Anti-preachy, anti-aesthetic-pantry framing.

scriptDraft.line: Sustainability content on TikTok is one of two things: a girl with a perfectly aesthetic pantry, or someone yelling at me about my coffee cup. I'm doing this for 30 days because I wanted a third option.
I'm not a sustainability person. I'm a creator-marketer who tried a 30-day challenge to see if structured habit-building actually changes anything when you're starting from average.
The product is Phobaxx. [Fill after G21 trial: one-liner product definition — what it literally is after hands-on trial].
Here's the thing — I'm going to post every day for 30 days. The honest version. The days I forget. The days I don't believe in this. The days something actually clicks. All of it.
If you're climate-curious and tired of preachy content, follow along. If at the end I don't think this worked, I'll tell you that too.

ctas.primary: Follow along for the full 30 days — I'll tell you if it doesn't work.
ctas.secondary: If you're tired of either the aesthetic-pantry camp or the guilt-trip camp, this one's for you.
